name: Browser build and verify
description: Test terminal/browser topology, DOM interaction, runtime diagnostics, and a bounded evidence-driven repair loop.

variants.description: Use a local two-page fixture to validate browser snapshot, interaction, wait, diagnostics, and screenshot evidence.
setup: Create a deterministic local site with a link, known DOM markers, a controlled console error toggle, and an allocated port.
Start the local server and create a run-owned terminal plus browser topology.
exercise: Navigate to the fixture, capture an interactive snapshot, activate the nonce-tagged link, wait for the target URL and DOM marker, and save a screenshot.
Enable the known console error, verify it appears in diagnostics, disable it, reload, and verify clean diagnostics.

assertions.expectation: The workspace contains the expected owned terminal and local-browser surfaces.
The snapshot exposes the nonce-tagged element and activation reaches the exact expected local URL and marker.
The known error is observed before repair and both console and error lists are clean afterward.
A non-empty screenshot artifact is associated with the final nonce-tagged page state.
The server, surfaces, screenshot, and fixture files are removed.

cleanup: Stop the local server, close the browser and terminal surfaces, and close the owned workspace.
Delete the fixture and screenshot after recording hashes required by the result.

variants.description: Let a real agent repair one seeded UI defect in an isolated worktree using machine-readable browser feedback.
setup: Create a disposable worktree containing a local app with exactly one seeded runtime defect, a known verifier, and an allocated port.
Launch one write-enabled agent only inside that worktree and create an owned browser surface after the listener is active.
exercise: Run the app, collect the known browser error, send the structured diagnostic to the agent, and allow at most three repair rounds.
After each round run tests plus browser diagnostics; stop only when both pass and capture final screenshot and diff evidence.

assertions.expectation: The pre-repair run observes the exact seeded runtime defect.
The repair loop performs no more than three rounds and every round is driven by captured diagnostics.
Tests pass, console and error lists are clean, and the expected DOM behavior works before success.
All modifications are confined to the owned worktree and the final diff addresses the seeded defect.
The agent, server, browser, worktree, and run-owned Cmux resources are removed after evidence collection.

cleanup: Stop the app and agent, close owned surfaces, and retain only the redacted diff and verifier summary.
Delete the disposable worktree and prove the parent repository is unchanged.
